enrichment.translation_en:
ROXANE:
Yes, I tremble, and I weep, and **I love you**, and I am yours!
And you have intoxicated me!
enrichment.larger_context_summary: In the balcony scene, Roxane speaks to Christian, the handsome young man she believes has been courting her with extraordinary eloquence. Unknown to her, Cyrano—who loves her but considers himself too ugly to be loved—is concealed nearby and has supplied Christian’s words, at points speaking in his place under cover of darkness. Roxane therefore sincerely directs her declaration toward Christian while responding emotionally to Cyrano’s language. The scene’s stakes lie in this divided romantic identity: she associates Christian’s appearance with the verbal and emotional depth that actually comes from Cyrano.
enrichment.interpretive_commentary: The target is principally a direct assertion of Roxane’s present emotional state, so its strong truth-conditional force is well supported. At the same time, the coordinated “and I am yours” gives the declaration a modest relationship-changing dimension: she is not merely describing affection but yielding herself to the bond. That performative coloring belongs especially to the surrounding continuation rather than to “I love you” alone. Her trembling, tears, exclamations, cumulative syntax, and intoxication metaphor make the avowal highly intense, but intensity is not the same as reflexive or non-propositional expressive force; the line remains a composed, intelligible claim. The balcony deception also does not make Roxane deceptive: she speaks sincerely, though she misidentifies the source of the eloquence that has moved her. This dramatic irony complicates the avowal’s relational object without changing its core semantic character.
